file_contents.pdd/tts_python.prompt:
Write a Python module that speaks a line of text aloud using the ElevenLabs
Text to Speech API.

Interface:

    speak(text: str, language_code: str, play: bool = True) -> Speech

    Speech is a dataclass with:
        audio_path: str            path to the written mp3
        duration_s: float

Implementation: use the official elevenlabs Python SDK, model
"eleven_multilingual_v2". Read ELEVENLABS_API_KEY from the environment; raise
a clear error at import time if absent.

Voice ids come from the environment: ELEVENLABS_VOICE_PATIENT and
ELEVENLABS_VOICE_DOCTOR, selected by which side is being spoken to. Accept the
voice id as an optional argument that overrides this. Never hardcode a voice id.

Write the mp3 to a temp file and return its path. When play is True, play it
through the default output device.

Text longer than 800 characters: do not truncate. Raise TtsError, and let the
caller decide.

Raise TtsError on API failure or timeout (15 second cap), with a message naming
the stage as "speech".

Use the current ElevenLabs Python SDK surface: instantiate
ElevenLabs(api_key=...) from elevenlabs.client, and synthesize via
client.text_to_speech.convert(voice_id=..., model_id=..., text=...), which
returns an iterator of audio bytes to be joined and written to file. Do not use
client.generate(), which no longer exists.
